matched_finding.subcategory: Lack of counterbalancing of critical discussed items
matched_finding.description: The manuscript states that 'each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase.' This means the discussed vs. non-discussed items are not counterbalanced across pairs. Any differences between discussed and non-discussed items could be due to item-specific characteristics (e.g., memorability, salience) rather than the effect of discussion/misinformation. This is a serious confound for the within-subjects comparison that forms the basis of the memory conformity effect measurement.
matched_finding.quote: In order to ensure sufficient discussion, each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase. For example, all pairs will talk about Eric's cap color and his company logo.

matched_finding.subcategory: Scoring rule ambiguity for discussed items
matched_finding.description: The analysis plan provides two different approaches to scoring discussed items. First, it describes a nuanced approach where only items where the partner actually provided discrepant information are classified as 'misleading.' Then it states 'we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation.' These are different scoring approaches that could yield different results, and the choice between them is not clearly justified or pre-committed.
matched_finding.quote: while scoring the individual memory test accuracy on the discussed questions (items containing misleading information), we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation, as the collaborative recall procedure is designed to expose participants to their partner's differing version of events.

The main reason for that is that we wanted to inoculate participants against the influence of misinformation before it could take eff...
ground_truth.description: Changed intervention from post- to pre-misinformation — tests encoding prevention instead of retrieval resistance; invalidates IMP theoretical framework which requires post-exposure placement

matched_finding.description: The authors place all three interventions (Extended warning, Education about memory, Demonstration and motivation) BEFORE the collaborative recall phase where misinformation is introduced. However, the theoretical framework (IMP, Blank 1998) and the rationale described in the introduction focus on participants who are 'aware of discrepancies between the original information and misinformation obtained from the partner.' At the time of the intervention, participants have not yet been exposed to misinformation, so there are no discrepancies to be aware of. This creates a fundamental mismatch between the theoretical mechanism (abandoning the consistency assumption after encountering discrepancies) and the procedural timing. The authors acknowledge this choice but the rationale ('inoculate participants against the influence of misinformation before it could take effect') is inconsistent with the IMP-based mechanism they describe.
matched_finding.quote: What is important, we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation before the collaborative recall phase (that is, before exposing participants to misinformation).

matched_finding.subcategory: Ruling out normative influence may be premature
matched_finding.description: The authors claim that 'normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect is completely ruled out in this study' because the individual memory test has no interpersonal pressure. However, normative influence during the collaborative recall phase could still affect encoding and consolidation of misinformation. The effects of normative pressure during discussion could carry over to the individual test even without direct social pressure at test time.
matched_finding.quote: we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect is completely ruled out in this study: participants work on their own and do not compare their answers with anybody

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Open-ended→forced-choice changes baseline conformity rate and scoring categories — must know format matters
ground_truth.original_snippet: In the present research, the individual memory test will be in the form of open-ended questions.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: In the present research, the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format.
ground_truth.description: Changed from open-ended to forced-choice — inflates conformity rates (50% guessing baseline vs much lower); scoring categories (correct, misinformation, other) don't make sense with forced-choice

matched_finding.description: The manuscript states in the Procedure section (2.5) that the individual memory test will contain '20 open-ended questions' and describes four indices derived from open-ended responses. However, in the Analysis Plan (Section 3), it states 'In the present research, the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format.' These are fundamentally incompatible test formats. The open-ended format allows for correct, misinformation-consistent, 'other,' and no-answer responses, while a two-alternative forced-choice format constrains responses to exactly two options. This contradiction makes it impossible to evaluate the validity of the planned analyses or to replicate the study.
matched_finding.quote: the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Co-witness exposure exclusion removed — must know non-exposed participants dilute the effect
ground_truth.original_snippet: In addition, participants who are not exposed to co-witness details at all (that is, the participants who did not hear any potentially misleading information from the partner) will be excluded from the analyses.
ground_truth.description: Removed exclusion of non-exposed participants — including those who received zero misinformation dilutes the conformity effect and biases against finding both the basic effect and intervention benefit
